anti_overlap: Does NOT cover prompt cache mechanics (handled by adjacent track)
Does NOT cover ranking pipelines for agents (fd-search-engine-ranking)
decision_lens: When the user has a goal, can they find the right slash command in under 3 seconds without typing more than the prefix, and does the system avoid surfacing irrelevant commands?
distance_rationale: IDE platforms and slash-command surfaces both face the same problem (large action catalog, user wants minimal-keystroke retrieval) but IDEs have refined this UX over 20+ years of feedback
expected_isomorphisms: Code-action ranking maps to slash-command listing order; intention grouping maps to command namespace UX; keyboard ergonomics maps to alias/shortcut design
focus: Reviews slash command discoverability, naming, and argument patterns through the lens of IDE quick-action UX — code-action ranking, intent classification, keyboard shortcut design
name: fd-ide-quick-actions
persona: Apply the perspective of an IDE platform designer (IntelliJ Code Actions, VSCode quick-fix, JetBrains intentions) — they care about action discoverability under context, ranking actions by relevance, suggestion fatigue from too many options, and keyboard-first ergonomics
review_areas: Prefix collision: how many slash commands share a 3-letter prefix (e.g., /clavain:* vs /interflux:*) — does typing the prefix narrow effectively?
Context relevance: when the user is in a sprint phase, are sprint-relevant commands ranked above unrelated ones in the listing?
Suggestion fatigue: 100+ commands in flat listing — does the user have to read all to find one?
Intent grouping: are commands grouped by user-intent verb (review, plan, ship, recall) or by plugin source?
Keyboard ergonomics: are the most-frequent commands (resolved via cass usage data) the shortest to type?
Argument hints: does the slash command surface accept `<args>` patterns that match user mental models, or require trial and error?

severity_examples.condition: User picks wrong command, wastes a turn, retries with another
severity_examples.scenario: Two slash commands have nearly identical names but different scopes (e.g., /clavain:review vs /code-review:code-review vs /pr-review-toolkit:review-pr) — user can't tell which to invoke

severity_examples.condition: Discoverability collapses; user falls back to `/help` or `cass search`
severity_examples.scenario: The user types a verb (`/recall`) but must remember the plugin namespace prefix

severity_examples.condition: Keyboard-first ergonomics inverted vs usage frequency
severity_examples.scenario: Frequently-used commands (per cass tool analytics) require more keystrokes than rarely-used ones

source_domain: IDE quick-action UX (IntelliJ Code Actions, VSCode commands)
success_hints: Cite specific command-name collisions and rank-disorder examples
Apply IDE intention-action ranking heuristics (recency, frequency, context-fit)
Recommend a verb-grouped or context-aware command listing
Reference cass usage data when proposing rank order
task_context: Sylveste exposes 100+ slash commands across plugins. Discoverability and naming follow no IDE-grade ranking discipline. Apply IDE quick-action playbook: rank by context relevance, group by intent, avoid suggestion fatigue, ensure prefixes don't collide. Identify the dominant discoverability gaps and propose ranking rules.
